newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina debt buyback possible, analysts say.
newsitem.headline: Argentina debt buyback possible, analysts say.

text.p: Argentina is ripe for a debt buyback similar to moves by other Latin American countries in the past week, analysts said.
The strongest argument for a buyback by Argentina is the large debt-servicing payments that fall due next year, estimated at $15 billion, they said.
"I think something will happen, but I don't know when or for how much," said Agustin Etchebarne, chief economist at private consultancy C&E Consultores.
Brazil's Congress passed a bill last week allowing the country to swap restructured Brady debt for global bonds.
On Monday, Mexico launched a 20-year bond priced to yield 445 basis points more than comparable U.S. Treasuries. On Tuesday, it increased the size of the issue.
Those moves boosted expectations that Argentina could raise the financing for a buyback.

"Sooner or later, the government will do it. I think the Argentine government is looking very closely at what other Latin American governments are doing," said Roberto Costa Bourdieu, senior fixed-income analyst at Banco Rio de la Plata.
The local bond market was abuzz on Monday with talk of a possible buyback.
Still, Deputy Finance Secretary Miguel Angel Kiguel told Reuters "that was just a rumor."

Analysts and traders said a buyback was possible because of Argentina's recent 375 million mark, 20-year bond issue. The government has also confirmed it was considering the launch of a 30-year bond as part of the remaining $4 billion of debt it wants to issue through the rest of the year. It said there had been offers to underwrite such an issue.
"The chances of a buyback increase as the offers increase," an analyst with a large foreign bank said:
To be sure, analysts are divided on what bonds are most likely to be bought back.
